REQ-005.requirement: OpenCode V2 plugins including UI behavior
REQ-005.conclusion: After excluding the separately guarded EXT-005 compatibility ambiguity and dependency-constrained UI-012, EXT-009 and EXT-012 remain requirement-identical. Requirement subtraction does not define which plugin lifecycle or UI-adjacent behavior belongs to either row.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: plugin id and Effect plugin activation callback within a location-scoped host
reviewedPartitions.outputs: active plugin scope, replacement/removal effects, wait completion, plugin-added event and replayed transformed state
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: load cycles and remove-while-loading die; activation defects close the child scope, are retained and are replayed to current/later waiters
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: location service keeps active child scopes, loading ids, waiters and retained failure exits until replacement/removal/finalization
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: one closeable child scope per active plugin plus keyed mutex/waiter maps; location finalizer closes the root plugin scope
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: This exact lifecycle is shared by every residual extensibility row through the same surface. No residual task card, requirement or pinned task-specific spec assigns it to EXT-004/006/009/010/011/012.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: configured package/file references, location config entries, plugin options and .opencode plugin files
reviewedPartitions.outputs: dynamically imported Effect/Promise plugin modules registered into the scoped plugin host
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: filesystem glob failures are softened, each package/import/decode/add sequence ignores its cause, and activation runs in a scoped background fiber
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: configured module discovery follows location/config lifetime; installed modules and dynamic imports belong to the JS/npm runtime
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: filesystem traversal, npm package resolution/install, dynamic JS import and background fibers
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: This partition requires the JS/npm runtime and package loading and has no task-specific residual owner. It is outside the authorized native lane unless new pinned ownership and runtime authority appear.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: location services spanning catalog, config, commands, skills, integrations, agents, references, models, filesystem and HTTP
reviewedPartitions.outputs: ordered built-in plugin registrations and replayable service transforms
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: registration runs inside a batched forked scope; downstream service/plugin failures retain their service-specific semantics
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: inherits all composed service scopes including HTTP/filesystem/npm/config resources
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The composition crosses many already-owned domains and cannot be treated as a catch-all EXT implementation. Skills/commands are separately guarded, integration auth has implemented ownership, and hook semantics remain frozen under EXT-008.

disqualifiers: Four generic residual rows are source-identical and two REQ-005 rows are requirement/source-identical.
Existing EXT-003/007 behavior and frozen EXT-008 hooks cannot be re-owned by subtraction.
The lifecycle spec explicitly leaves reload/watch and deferred external activation as design work, so broader plugin parity is not established.

historyReview.limitation: Current pinned source/caller/test/spec evidence is authoritative for behavior; unavailable historical intent is not used to map generic residual ids.

closureCriteria: Each residual EXT owner requires direct task-specific source, caller, direct test and genuine spec evidence that distinguishes it from its equivalence peers; list order, task number, REQ-005 subtraction and surface membership are insufficient.

External plugin work must explicitly own JS/npm/package-install/network authority, module validation/failure policy, cache/update lifetime and location-scope cleanup before a native implementation is attempted.
Existing EXT-001/002 guards, EXT-003/007 implementations, EXT-005 compatibility ambiguity, EXT-008 hook blocker and UI-012 dependency constraint must remain excluded.
All unresolved partitions and design gaps must receive task-specific dispositions or remain explicitly blocked before the extensibility family can be called decomposed.
